findings.reason: Clause (i) calls F a force model of post-cm02-force-superposition but allows F only on an arbitrary open D; the supplier defines its force map on I0×Q×R^(3N). State that D carries a restriction of the full supplier map, and ensure periodic domains are preserved under time shifts.

Clause (v) defines a homoclinic orbit only by the two limiting conditions, so the constant equilibrium motion qualifies. Require a nonconstant motion to align with the nontrivial homoclinic-point definition used by the horseshoe supplier.

Clause (iii) declares a matrix-valued Y but sets Y(0)=u for a vector and later takes a vector norm; specify either a vector solution with initial value u or a matrix solution with initial value I. Clause (vi)(a) is false: a hyperbolic sink such as A=-I is linearly stable.

Clause (vi)(b) says equilibrium eigenvalues can change under a nonlinear chart transition. At an equilibrium, a smooth chart change conjugates the derivative by its Jacobian, so the eigenvalues are unchanged.

The Units remark repeats the claim that equilibrium linearization eigenvalues are chart-dependent. Correct it to distinguish the invariant spectrum from norm-dependent growth bounds and chart-dependent finite-time rates.

Proof step 3.1 repeats the incorrect claim that a general nonlinear chart transition can change the eigenvalues of the derivative at an equilibrium. The spectrum is invariant under the similarity transformation induced by the chart change.

Clause (i) calls a stroboscopic fixed point a P-periodic state but only states equality where both solution values are defined. Show that periodic forcing and uniqueness glue the segment to a complete periodic motion on R, or use a term restricted to the segment.

Clause (b) says fixed coordinate rescaling can change the four chaos properties; such rescaling is a bi-Lipschitz conjugacy, which preserves the topological clauses and sensitivity. The claim that all four properties are independent is also not established by the examples given; qualify it or supply the claimed nonimplications.

The Statement calls the torus map continuous and then uses its derivatives and Lagrangian pullback. The KAM supplier's proof supplies angular derivative convergence; state at least C1 regularity explicitly in the consuming claim.

Clause (i) sets the one-label configuration domain to R and calls it a model of post-cm02-force-superposition, whose one-label configuration domain is an open subset of R^3. Present this as a separately adopted reduced-coordinate model or give an explicit framework embedding. Clause (iii) also includes constant codes as homoclinic points, although the mathematical supplier requires nonconstant codes. In clause (iv)/proof 4.1, derive backward and all-time existence from the shift conjugacy and periodicity rather than only forward stroboscopic invariance.

Proof steps 1.1 and 2.1 use phase-volume preservation for every real t and the time-one map on A, while pthm-cm13-liouville and pthm-cm13-flow-preservation establish preservation on local time-slice domains. Supply the finite-cover/subdivision argument along the compact invariant closure of A, or state the exact all-time preservation result needed.

The refuted conclusion applies the page's chaos predicate to a flow, while that predicate is defined only for maps. Specify a map, such as the time-one map on a compact invariant set, and prove the corresponding counterexample.

The physical_scope describes a one-dimensional model and a phase-area bound, but the Example uses a one-label R^3 model and a six-dimensional volume bound. Also, the free trajectory may return finitely to a bounded set containing its initial state; replace “never returns” with the valid eventual-exit/no-infinite-return claim.

Sections 1 and 3 say every theorem uses the force-model class of def-cm16-flow and that the hyperbolic-linearization theorem is finite-time; the rotor, pulsed oscillator and general mechanical-chart statements use separately declared model classes, and the hyperbolic theorem includes all-time local exponential stability and instability conclusions. Correct the summary and its repeated chart-spectrum claim.
